## Disposition: not_a_bug — operator decision 2026-08-05

Closing on the investigation recorded above. The four Acceptance Criteria are INVESTIGATIVE
(trace / explain / determine / conditional), and each is answered — the answer is that the
reported condition does not exist:

- AC1 (trace each of the six to the producer that minted its attestation): none of the six has
  a FORCE_CLOSE audit record at all. A real record is a comment whose body starts
  `FORCE_CLOSE:` (src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:435-441). Their attestations came
  from the ordinary close path. The original scan substring-matched serialized event JSON and
  caught LLM prose that merely QUOTED the string.
- AC2 (explain e95e's signature-before-force-close ordering, or confirm a defect): explained,
  not a defect. The matched "force" is a snapshot of e95e's OWN description text, which reads
  "there is NO REOPEN/FORCE_CLOSE event type". There was no force-close event to order against.
- AC3 (determine whether any of the six is a child whose parent's certification depended on it):
  no integrity exposure by mechanism. `child_closure_findings`
  (src/rebar/llm/completion.py:89-103) checks signature VALIDITY, not mere presence, so a
  force-closed or reopened child is treated as uncertified and withholds the parent's signature.
- AC4 (if the op-cert service can mint a completion cert for a FORCED close, then...): the
  antecedent is false, so the conditional is discharged. Force-close has NEVER been able to sign:
  src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:176-177 returns None on `force_close` BEFORE the
  disposition branch, and signing occurs only when that result is non-None. `git log -S` places
  the guard in the commit that INTRODUCED the close gate (2026-06-18).

Empirical confirmation from today: 43ea-3d5a-078f-4fe3 was deliberately force-closed and
carries two `certifiable: true` COMPLETION_VERDICT events and ZERO completion-verifier
attestation — exactly the correct behavior.

Correction worth recording: 738a-376e-4829-42ca is NOT the fix for this. Its change
(adc0b64a2b, today) added disposition-close attestation and mutation-checked the pre-existing
guard, but does not touch the force_close line. The guard predates it by roughly six weeks.

The genuine population of force-closed-then-signed tickets is 13 and is DISJOINT from the six
named here; seven show the documented reopen -> re-close remedy. The remaining six predate the
`last_reopened_at` field (added 2026-06-30), so their pre-close history was compacted away —
recorded as inference, not verification.

Methodology note for future audits: match STRUCTURED records, not substrings in serialized
event JSON, or LLM prose quoting a marker will be counted as the marker. Also, compiled
comments use key `body`, not `text` — a scan keyed on `text` silently returns zero results.
